provenance.notes: AUTHORED, NOT RECORDED. No ACP agent is installed on the recording host, so every frame in this file is written against the Agent Client Protocol schema at github.com/zed-industries/agent-client-protocol, schema/v1 (meta.json reports version 1), and provenance.source is "authored" rather than "recorded". `provenance.version` is the ACP PROTOCOL version this fixture targets -- the integer 1 that `initialize` negotiates -- not a CLI release. v1 is targeted rather than v2 because v1 is the version that carries `session/load`, which is the method the resume path is specified against; v2 replaces it with `session/resume`. WIRE SHAPE: ACP is line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio in BOTH directions, so unlike Codex every frame here carries "jsonrpc":"2.0". `session/update` and `session/cancel` are notifications (no id); `session/request_permission` is an agent->client REQUEST and carries an id that must be answered. Paths are already at the TRANSCRIPT_PLACEHOLDERS values -- workspace /tmp/agent-workspace, home /home/agent, username agent -- since nothing here came off a real machine. CAPABILITY NEGOTIATION -- two variants exist and Task 4 derives a descriptor from each. acp-completes.json is the FULL negotiation: `agentCapabilities.loadSession: true` (so resume: true), permission support advertised, `promptCapabilities` and `mcpCapabilities` populated, and a `session/new` result carrying `modes` (SessionModeState) and `configOptions` for model and reasoning selection, which is where D-9's selection.modelSelection and selection.reasoningSelection come from. acp-completes-minimal.json is the MINIMAL negotiation: loadSession false, no permission advertisement, no modes, no configOptions -- from which the descriptor must derive resume: false, permissions: false, empty permissionModes, both selection flags false, and the returned harness must have no `respondToPermission` property at all. CAVEAT, IMPORTANT: ACP v1 has NO standard capability flag for permission prompting. Any agent may send `session/request_permission` at any time; the schema's AgentCapabilities carries only loadSession, promptCapabilities, mcpCapabilities, sessionCapabilities and auth. That key is an AutoStack convention, not part of ACP. Task 4 must treat its ABSENCE as permissions: false (fail closed), which is exactly what the minimal variant exercises. D-3 ORDERING: the `session/request_permission` REQUEST is the first frame mentioning this tool call, and no `session/update` of kind `tool_call` or `tool_call_update` for call_01hq8p42 appears before the `awaitStdin` that represents the decision. The gated `tool_call` (status in_progress) and the diff-bearing `tool_call_update` both arrive after it, so behaviour 4's no-side-effect-before-the-decision assertion holds by construction. The `toolCall` object embedded in the permission request is a ToolCallUpdate carried as DATA inside the ask, not a tool_call notification -- it must not be mapped to a `tool_call` event. OPTIONS: all four PermissionOptionKind values are offered (allow_once, allow_always, reject_once, reject_always), so the contract's must-offer-a-denial refinement is satisfied twice over. The client answers with {"outcome":{"outcome":"selected","optionId":"allow-once"}}; the other legal outcome is {"outcome":{"outcome":"cancelled"}}, which a client MUST send for every pending permission request when it cancels the turn. Permission capability is not advertised by ACP v1 at all; per plan decision D-12 it is derived from the configured launch profile rather than from an invented protocol extension.
